C0.quote: the alternative is accepted if it garners at least k
C0.note: Committee voting under k-majority rule with strategic voting.

C1.quote: we solve for symmetric (Bayesian-Nash) equilibria of the voting game
C1.note: WD because the principal's expected payoff, equivalent to utilitarian welfare (fn 9), is used to evaluate committee composition.

C2.2.note: Binary Yes/No vote on a single alternative against the status quo.

C2.3.quote: which yields a private signal θ i
C2.3.note: Experts hold private signals and interdependent payoffs.

C2.4.quote: Expert i is said to vote sincerely if he conditions his vote
C2.4.note: Votes are determined by cutoff strategies on signals; equilibrium cutoffs generally differ from sincere voting.

C3.1.note: Every main analysis uses equilibrium (strategic) voting by experts. The optimal-voting benchmark, in which the principal dictates cutoffs, is not an analysis of voters submitting held attitudes.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH (binary votes), so the applicability condition is not met.

C5.1.quote: This is equivalent to assuming a utilitarian principal for the alternative
C5.1.note: The principal's payoff (average quality, equivalent to utilitarian welfare) is evaluated in Propositions 3, 5 and 6.

C5.2.quote: cares about the average quality of the alternative
C5.2.note: Evaluated on the signals and payoffs, not on the votes.

VOT.quote_info: The interdependence parameter β 2 [0, 1] is commonly known
VOT.note: Experts know their own signal and the common prior distribution F.

ORG.quote_behav: we ask whether an uninformed principal would appoint more or less
ORG.quote_info: her ex ante payoff before a committee vote is:
ORG.note: The principal chooses committee composition (β), information (λ) and size. She has no signals but evaluates ex ante payoffs using the prior F, so she knows a prior; this is inferable from the model rather than said in words.

C7.1.quote: the principal may try to influence their equilibrium voting
C7.1.note: Both present types (voters and principal) are strategic.

C8.1.quote: we solve for symmetric (Bayesian-Nash) equilibria of the voting game
C8.1.note: SPE: the principal chooses composition, information and size anticipating the equilibrium voting, which is a backward-induction structure; this concept is not named explicitly.

claims.quote: the principal may sometimes raise – not lower – the cost
the principal may not consult an informed expert for every attribute
the principal may prefer some members to be uninformed

C9.1.note: Claims about how organisations should design committees.

C9.2.quote: Upon receiving their private signals, committee members simultaneously vote
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions are stated: strategic experts, private signals with a common prior, interdependent payoffs, the principal's status quo bias, and abstentions counting as No votes.

C3.1.reason: All main results characterise equilibrium voting, and the dictated-cutoff benchmark is not a non-strategic voter analysis, so ALL applies.

C3.2.reason: With C3.1 = ALL, the codebook requires NA.

C3.3.reason: With C3.2 not STATED, the codebook requires NA.

C6.ORG.reason: Knowing only the prior counts as PARTIAL under the codebook, but that knowledge is only inferable from the ex ante payoff formulation, so info_stated is IMPLICIT.

C8.1.reason: The principal's choice made in anticipation of equilibrium play is backward induction, which the codebook codes as SPE rather than OTH or omitting it.
